title: Historical Simulation and Bayesian Analysis Summary
paragraphs: Appendix C Historical Simulation and Bayesian Analysis Summary This appendix preserves the original study's model-analysis summary. G0 and G1 identify engagement-rst and epistemic-rst congurations. The supplied R les do not contain a registration identier or a dated blinding log. Accordingly, the summary is not presented as evidence of completed preregistration or veried blinding; those procedural records are separate from the numerical results. C.1 Primary Endpoints The primary endpoints of the arm contrast are: (1) the PB composite dierence (G1 minus G0); (2) the BRS aggregate dierence; (3) the ve-point star-rating dierence; and (4) the raw engagement dierence. The specied expectations are: positive PB, BRS, and star dierences in the direction EST-P1 predicts; an engagement decrease of the size EST-P2 predicts; and a reported trade-o index, interpreted in its component metric units. 257

APPENDIX C. HISTORICAL SIMULATION AND BAYESIAN ANALYSIS SUMMARY 258 C.2 Results Counterfactual eects (G1 minus G0, N = 52 substrate): PB composite +0.511 [0.507, 0.514]; information quality +0.131; broadcaster rigor +0.051; social validation +0.003; star rating +0.165 [0.104, 0.204]; echo/density +0.035; correction acceptance +0.026; raw engagement −0.217; continued listening −0.054. The historical contrast table records p = .0001 for each dierence; these entries concern the model analysis, not a randomised eld experiment. The reported engagementversus-epistemic trade-o index is −0.290. Calibration against the rened sample: weighted Wasserstein loss 0.0406 (G0) and 0.0178 (G1) against a target of 0.04. Sensitivity: all 48 design points of the Latin-hypercube sweep support the ve model mechanism checks. Bayesian update (PyMC, N = 52): information quality β = 0.786, 95% equal-tailed credible interval [0.670, 0.910]; maximum bR = 1.008; minimum eective sample size 606; posterior predictive coverage 0.96; posterior predictive mean 5.115 against the observed mean 5.119. Predictor Pearson collinearity (BRIQ r = 0.861) limits interpretation of a uniquely identiable quality mechanism. Coecients refer to standardized predictors; predictive coverage is in-sample. The historical eect bounds are central replication-percentile intervals, not mean-eect condence intervals (Section 6.11).
